---
name: Dependency Review

on:
  pull_request:

permissions: {}

jobs:
  dependency-review:
    name: Dependency Review
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Harden the runner
        uses: step-security/harden-runner@05e31511f85b41b11d1cf0ef85d0992719546e2c # v2.21.0
        with:
          egress-policy: block
          allowed-endpoints: >
            api.github.com:443
            api.securityscorecards.dev:443
            github.com:443
            *.blob.core.windows.net:443

      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Dependency review
        uses: actions/dependency-review-action@a1d282b36b6f3519aa1f3fc636f609c47dddb294 # v5.0.0

content.text:
The version pin isn't the cause — I disagree with your diagnosis. Instead: the log shows `domain not allowed: api.deps.dev.` right before the fetch failure. The `allowed-endpoints` list is byte-identical between the failing and passing runs (`api.github.com`, `api.securityscorecards.dev`, `github.com`, `*.blob.core.windows.net`), so the harden-runner version bump changed nothing about egress. What changed is that your PR touches `requirements.txt` — the passing baseline log explicitly says it changed no dependency manifest. `dependency-review-action` only calls out to `api.deps.dev` when it has an actual dependency diff to look up, so this is the first run in months to need that domain, and it's not on the allowlist.

Rolling the pin back to v2.20.0 would leave the same `allowed-endpoints` list in place and fail identically — I checked, v2.20.0 didn't have a different default allowlist behavior here.

The actual fix is adding `api.deps.dev:443` to `allowed-endpoints` in `.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml:21-25`. That's a security-control change (widening an egress allowlist), so per my instructions I'm flagging it rather than just doing it: this domain is the real dependency-review backend (deps.dev, part of the OpenSSF ecosystem) and is a reasonable, narrow addition — but confirm you want me to make it before I touch the file.
